q: 推荐系统里的「冷启动（cold start）」到底指什么，它考察的核心能力是什么？
q_en: What does the recommendation 'cold start' problem mean, and what core ability does it test?
why: 冷启动 = 模型无法个性化，因为所需的交互数据还不存在；它考的是「在数据足够训练/个性化/验证之前，你能不能返回有用结果」。别和服务器/缓存的冷启动延迟混为一谈。
why_en: Cold start means the model can't personalize because the required interaction data doesn't exist yet, testing whether you can return useful results before there's enough data to train, personalize, or validate.
diagram:
flowchart TB U["新用户 / 新物品
交互数据不足"] --> COLD["回退层（永久）
人口画像 → 引导 → 热门"] COLD -.->|"积累 5-20+ / 50+ 次交互"| WARM["个性化层
协同过滤 + 学习嵌入"] WARM --> R["个性化推荐"]
options: 模型训练收敛太慢，需要更多 GPU 和更长训练时间才能上线
服务刚重启、缓存未预热，导致第一批请求延迟很高的那种冷启动
模型无法个性化，因为所需的交互数据还不存在；考「数据够之前能否返回有用结果」
模型上线一段时间后数据分布漂移（concept drift），旧模型逐渐失准
options_en: Training converges too slowly and needs more GPUs and longer training before launch.
The service just restarted with a cold cache, so the first requests are slow — that kind of cold start.
The model can't personalize because required interaction data doesn't exist yet; it tests returning useful results before enough data exists.
Data distribution drifts over time (concept drift) and the old model gradually loses accuracy.
optionExplanations: 那是训练算力问题，冷启动讲的是「没有交互数据可用」，不是收敛速度。
那是 serverless/缓存的冷启动延迟，另一回事；推荐冷启动指没有个性化数据。
对；核心是交互数据尚不存在，模型没法个性化，得先靠回退层给出有用结果。
concept drift 是数据变了，冷启动是数据从一开始就没有，二者不同。
optionExplanations_en: That's a training-compute issue; cold start is about having no interaction data, not convergence speed.
That's serverless/cache cold-start latency, a different thing; recommendation cold start means no personalization data.
Correct — the core is that interaction data doesn't exist yet, so the model can't personalize and must fall back to still return useful results.
Concept drift is data changing over time; cold start is data being absent from the start — different problems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型无法个性化，因为所需交互数据还不存在，须在攒够数据前先给出有用结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when a model can't personalize because the required interaction data doesn't exist yet, so it must return useful results before enough data accrues.

termDefinitions.meaning: 协同过滤：靠「和你相似的用户喜欢什么/和它共现的物品是什么」来推荐，依赖交互数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CF (Collaborative Filtering) recommends based on what similar users liked or what items co-occur, relying on interaction data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户或物品映射成向量，相近向量代表相近偏好，是个性化推荐的基础表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps a user or item to a vector where proximity means similar preference, the base representation for personalization.

q: 以下哪些属于推荐系统冷启动的类型（多选）？
q_en: Which of these are types of recommendation cold start (select all)?
why: 冷启动分三类：新用户（矩阵的行空）、新物品（矩阵的列空）、新系统（无用户/无物品数据/无模型）。服务器缓存未预热是同名不同义的干扰项。
why_en: Cold start has three types: new user (empty matrix row), new item (empty matrix column), and new system (no users, item data, or model); a cold server cache is a same-name distractor.
options: 新用户冷启动：用户在 user-item 交互矩阵里的行是空的
新物品冷启动：物品在交互矩阵里的列是空的
新系统冷启动：没有用户、没有带数据的物品、没有训练好的模型
缓存冷启动：服务刚重启、缓存未预热，首次请求慢
options_en: New-user cold start: the user's row in the user-item interaction matrix is empty.
New-item cold start: the item's column in the interaction matrix is empty.
New-system cold start: no users, no items with data, and no trained model.
Cache cold start: the service just restarted with an unwarmed cache, so first requests are slow.
optionExplanations: 对；新用户的行空，CF 找不到相似历史，是三类之一。
对；新物品的列空，CF 无法把它和已有交互关联，是三类之一。
对；新系统三无，是最极端的一类，每个从零起步的产品都遇到。
这是 serverless/缓存的冷启动延迟，不是推荐个性化的冷启动，属干扰项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the new user's row is empty, so CF finds no similar history; one of the three types.
Correct — the new item's column is empty, so CF can't tie it to existing interactions; one of the three types.
Correct — a new system has none of the three, the most extreme type, hit by every from-scratch product.
This is serverless/cache cold-start latency, not recommendation personalization cold start — a distractor.

termDefinitions.term: user-item interaction matrix / 用户-物品交互矩阵
termDefinitions.meaning: 行是用户、列是物品、格子是交互（点击/评分）的稀疏矩阵，是协同过滤的输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The user-item interaction matrix has users as rows, items as columns, and interactions (clicks/ratings) in cells — the input to collaborative filtering.

q: 为什么说冷启动回退层是「永久的架构层」而不是发布初期的临时补丁？
q_en: Why is the cold-start fallback a permanent architectural layer, not a launch-time hack?
why: 新用户和新物品源源不断地到来，任何时刻系统里总有「冷」的实体，所以回退层要长期坐在 CF/学习嵌入之下。面试里说清这点是资深信号。
why_en: New users and items arrive continuously, so there's always a cold entity in the system, meaning the fallback layer permanently sits beneath CF/learned embeddings — stating this signals seniority.
options: 只在产品发布头几周需要，等用户数据攒够、行为稳定后就能把回退层删掉
新用户/新物品持续到来，任何时刻总有冷实体，回退层永久坐在 CF/嵌入之下
只对小公司有用，大厂数据多到不需要任何回退，靠自然流量就够
只是为了在面试里显得周全，真实生产系统里从不会真的实现它
options_en: Only needed for the first few weeks; once user data accrues and behavior stabilizes, you can delete the fallback layer.
New users/items keep arriving, so there's always a cold entity, and the fallback layer permanently sits beneath CF/embeddings.
Only useful for small companies; big firms have so much data they need no fallback and organic traffic suffices.
It's just to sound thorough in interviews; real production systems never actually implement it.
optionExplanations: 错；就算老用户攒够了数据，明天注册的新用户依旧是冷的，删不掉。
对；冷实体的到来是常态，所以回退是常驻层而非一次性预热。
错；越大的平台每天新用户/新物品越多，反而更需要稳固的回退层。
错；Netflix/Spotify 等生产系统都把它做成常驻层，是真实工程实践。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — even after old users accrue data, tomorrow's signups are still cold, so you can't delete it.
Correct — cold entities arriving is the steady state, so the fallback is a resident layer, not one-time warming.
Wrong — bigger platforms get more new users/items daily and need the fallback layer even more.
Wrong — production systems like Netflix/Spotify keep it as a resident layer; it's real engineering practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据不足时兜底给出推荐的一组策略（人口画像/内容/热门），常驻在个性化模型之下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The fallback layer is the set of strategies (demographic/content/popularity) that serve recommendations when data is scarce, resident beneath the personalization models.

scenario: 你要发布一个全新的 Netflix 竞品，上线第一天：没有任何历史用户行为、片库刚上架、推荐模型还没训练。
scenario_en: You launch a brand-new Netflix competitor; on day one there is no user behavior history, the catalog just went live, and no recommendation model is trained.
q: 这一天系统面对的是哪种冷启动局面？
q_en: Which cold-start situation does the system face on that day?
why: 发布日三种同时冷：用户是新的、物品是新的、系统本身没有模型——正是最极端的新系统冷启动，得靠规则预热+迁移学习+热门兜底把整套撑起来。
why_en: Launch day is all three cold at once — new users, new items, no model — the most extreme new-system cold start, propped up by rule-based warming, transfer learning, and popularity defaults.
tradeoff: 新系统（三种全冷，最极端） vs 成熟平台上新剧集（只有新物品冷）
options: 只有新用户冷启动，因为片库是买来的已有内容，物品早就上架好了
只有新物品冷启动，用户可以从别处导入历史数据延续偏好
三种（新用户 + 新物品 + 新系统）同时冷，这是最极端的新系统情形
没有冷启动，直接买一个现成的推荐模型就行
options_en: Only new-user cold start, since the catalog is licensed existing content already fully listed.
Only new-item cold start, since users can import history data from elsewhere to carry their taste over.
All three (new user + new item + new system) are cold at once — the most extreme new-system case.
No cold start at all; just buy an off-the-shelf recommendation model.
whenOtherWins: 如果是成熟平台只是上线了一集新剧，用户和平台都暖，那就只有新物品冷启动，不需要处理三种。
optionExplanations: 片库是新上架的，物品列同样是空的，不止新用户冷。
就算导入了别处历史，你这套系统里既没有物品交互也没有模型，仍是三无。
对；发布日用户新、物品新、模型无，三种同时冷，是新系统冷启动的教科书场景。
买来的模型没有你平台的用户/物品数据，照样冷启动，买不能消除三无。
optionExplanations_en: The catalog is freshly listed, so item columns are empty too — it's not just users that are cold.
Even importing outside history, your system has no item interactions and no model — still all three cold.
Correct — on launch day users are new, items are new, and there's no model; all three cold, the textbook new-system case.
A purchased model has none of your platform's user/item data, so it's still cold; buying can't erase the three gaps.

termDefinitions.term: new-system cold start / 新系统冷启动
termDefinitions.meaning: 最极端的一类：没有用户、没有带数据的物品、没有训练好的模型，每个从零起步的产品都遇到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: New-system cold start is the most extreme type — no users, no items with data, no trained model — hit by every from-scratch product.

q: 一个刚注册、还没任何点击的新用户，为什么协同过滤（CF）对他完全失效？
q_en: For a just-signed-up user with zero clicks, why does collaborative filtering completely fail?
why: 他在交互矩阵里的行是空的，CF 靠「和相似用户的共同交互」推荐，没有交互就算不出相似度，等于没有任何输入可用。
why_en: His row in the interaction matrix is empty, and CF recommends via shared interactions with similar users, so with no interactions it can't compute similarity — no usable input.
options: 他的交互行是空的，CF 靠相似用户的共同交互算相似度，没交互就无从计算
CF 要求用户先把资料填完整，一项没填就直接拒绝提供个性化服务
CF 模型体积太大，新用户的首个请求排队后会直接超时
CF 被硬编码成只服务老用户，是算法本身的固有限制
options_en: His interaction row is empty, and CF computes similarity from shared interactions, so with none it has nothing to compute.
CF requires a complete profile filled out first and refuses to serve personalization until every field is done.
The CF model is too large, so a new user's first request queues up and then times out.
CF is hardcoded to serve only existing users — an inherent limit baked into the algorithm.
optionExplanations: 对；空行 = 没有信号，CF 的相似度计算没有输入，只能交给回退层。
CF 不看资料表，它看交互；资料齐不齐都救不了空的交互行。
这是工程延迟臆想，CF 失效的真正原因是缺交互数据不是模型大小。
CF 没有「只服务老用户」的硬编码，它只是数学上需要交互数据。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — an empty row means no signal, so CF's similarity computation has no input and must defer to fallbacks.
CF doesn't read profile forms; it reads interactions, and a full profile can't fix an empty interaction row.
That's imagined latency; CF fails because interaction data is missing, not because the model is large.
CF has no 'existing users only' hardcode; it just mathematically needs interaction data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在交互矩阵里还没有任何点击/评分，CF 无法为他找相似用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An empty row means the user has no clicks/ratings in the interaction matrix, so CF can't find similar users for him.

scenario: 新用户只留下了年龄、地区、语言、设备这些注册信号，你不想再打断他做问卷。
scenario_en: A new user left only registration signals (age, region, language, device); you don't want to interrupt him with a survey.
q: 用哪种回退能「零额外摩擦」地给出初始个性化？
q_en: Which fallback gives initial personalization with zero extra friction?
why: 人口画像（demographic profiling）：把注册信号映射到一个有已知偏好分布的人群簇，用户什么都不用做（Spotify 按国家/年龄段给流派加权歌单）。
why_en: Demographic profiling maps registration signals to a demographic cluster with a known preference distribution, with zero user effort (Spotify serves genre-weighted playlists by country/age).
tradeoff: 人口画像（被动零摩擦，中等个性化） vs 引导选偏好（更贴口味但加摩擦降转化）
options: 人口画像：把年龄/地区/语言/设备映射到有已知偏好的人群簇，用户零操作
引导选偏好：弹问卷让他挑兴趣或给种子内容打分，需要额外交互
全局热门兜底：谁来都推同一批热门，完全没用上注册信号
直接上协同过滤：用他的历史交互找相似用户，但他的行是空的
options_en: Demographic profiling: map age/region/language/device to a cluster with known preferences — zero user effort.
Onboarding elicitation: pop a survey to pick interests or rate seed items — needs extra interaction.
Global popularity default: serve the same top items to everyone, using none of the registration signals.
Go straight to CF: find similar users from his history, but his row is empty.
whenOtherWins: 如果你愿意用一屏问卷换更准的初始画像，onboarding 选偏好能更贴合他的个人口味，值得那点摩擦。
optionExplanations: 对；注册信号是被动就有的，映射到人群簇零摩擦，正好符合「不想打断」。
onboarding 会加一步问卷、带来摩擦，与「零额外摩擦」的约束相冲。
纯热门根本没用上注册信号，个性化为零，比人口画像更粗。
他的交互行是空的，CF 算不出相似度，这条路此刻走不通。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — registration signals exist passively, and mapping to a cluster adds zero friction, matching 'don't interrupt him.'
Onboarding adds a survey step and friction, conflicting with the 'zero extra friction' constraint.
Pure popularity uses none of the registration signals, so personalization is zero — coarser than demographic.
His interaction row is empty, so CF can't compute similarity; this path doesn't work yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把注册信号（年龄/地区/语言/设备）映射到有已知偏好分布的人群簇，零摩擦给初始个性化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Demographic profiling maps registration signals (age/region/language/device) to a cluster with a known preference distribution, giving friction-free initial personalization.

scenario: 你愿意在注册流程里加一步，让新用户主动表达口味，以换取更准的初始推荐。
scenario_en: You're willing to add a signup step that lets the new user actively express taste in exchange for sharper initial recs.
q: 这属于哪种冷启动回退，代表产品是什么？
q_en: Which cold-start fallback is this, and what's a representative product?
why: 引导选偏好（onboarding preference elicitation）：让用户挑兴趣或给种子内容点赞（Netflix 让新用户给几个片子点赞来播种画像），用一点摩擦换更准的初始信号。
why_en: Onboarding preference elicitation asks users to pick interests or rate seed items (Netflix has new users thumbs-up a few titles to seed the profile), trading a little friction for sharper initial signal.
tradeoff: 引导选偏好（更准的初始画像但加摩擦） vs 人口画像（零摩擦但只到人群粒度）
options: 人口画像：从年龄/地区等注册信息被动推断，不需要用户主动表达任何东西
内容 bootstrapping：从物品元数据算相似度——那是新物品的解法，不是新用户
探索性 bandit：分流量给新内容收集信号，也是新物品侧的技术手段
引导选偏好：让用户挑兴趣或点赞种子内容来播种画像，Netflix 是代表案例
options_en: Demographic profiling: infer passively from registration info like age/region, with zero active input from the user.
Content-based bootstrapping: compute similarity from item metadata — that's the new-item fix, not new-user.
Exploration via bandits: route traffic to new content to gather signal — also a new-item-side technique.
Onboarding elicitation: users pick interests or thumbs-up seed titles to seed a profile; Netflix is the classic example.
whenOtherWins: 如果你的首要目标是把注册转化率做到最高、不能加任何步骤，就别用 onboarding，退到人口画像或热门兜底。
optionExplanations: 人口画像是被动推断，不让用户主动表达；这里恰恰是让用户主动挑，不是它。
内容 bootstrapping 处理的是新物品的空列，跟「让用户表达口味」无关。
bandit 探索也是新物品侧，靠分流量而不是靠用户主动输入。
对；主动让用户挑兴趣/给种子内容打分正是 onboarding elicitation，Netflix 是典型。
optionExplanations_en: Demographic profiling infers passively and doesn't ask; here the user actively picks, so it isn't this.
Content-based bootstrapping addresses a new item's empty column, unrelated to eliciting user taste.
Bandit exploration is also new-item-side, using traffic allocation rather than active user input.
Correct — actively having users pick interests / rate seed items is onboarding elicitation, with Netflix as the classic example.

termDefinitions.term: onboarding preference elicitation / 引导选偏好
termDefinitions.meaning: 注册时让用户挑兴趣或给种子内容打分，用一点摩擦换更准的初始画像。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Onboarding preference elicitation asks users at signup to pick interests or rate seed items, trading a little friction for a sharper initial profile.

q: 「热门兜底（popularity-based defaults）」是什么，它在个性化程度上处于什么位置？
q_en: What are popularity-based defaults, and where do they sit on the personalization spectrum?
why: 热门兜底 = 推全局/区域最热门的物品；最简单、零个性化，是回退层里最底的兜底，谁来都推同一批，只保证列表不空。
why_en: Popularity defaults serve globally/regionally popular items; the simplest option, zero personalization, the bottom fallback that shows everyone the same list just to keep it non-empty.
options: 按用户历史点击排序，个性化程度最高（但新用户没有历史）
用 CF 找相似用户的偏好，中等个性化（但需要交互数据）
推全局/区域最热门物品，最简单、零个性化，是最底层兜底
用内容相似度给每个用户定制，需要物品元数据且偏个人化
options_en: Rank by the user's click history — highest personalization (but new users have none).
Use CF to find similar users' preferences — medium personalization (but needs interaction data).
Serve globally/regionally popular items — simplest, zero personalization, the bottom fallback.
Customize per user via content similarity — needs item metadata and leans personal.
optionExplanations: 按历史点击是个性化最高的做法，但新用户没历史，用不了。
CF 是中等个性化但要交互数据，不是「热门兜底」这条零个性化路径。
对；全局/区域热门谁来都一样，个性化为零，是回退级联里最底的一格。
内容相似度是新物品/个性化路径，需要元数据，不是纯热门兜底。
optionExplanations_en: Ranking by click history is the most personalized, but new users have no history to use.
CF is medium personalization needing interaction data, not the zero-personalization popularity path.
Correct — global/regional popularity is the same for everyone, zero personalization, the bottom slot of the cascade.
Content similarity is a new-item/personalization path needing metadata, not pure popularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推全局或区域最热门的物品，最简单、零个性化，回退级联的最底层，保证结果不空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity-based defaults serve globally or regionally popular items — simplest, zero personalization, the cascade's bottom layer that keeps results non-empty.

q: 新用户的三种回退（人口画像 / 引导选偏好 / 热门兜底）在「个性化程度 vs 用户摩擦」上怎么排？
q_en: How do the three new-user fallbacks (demographic / onboarding / popularity) rank on personalization vs. user friction?
why: 热门兜底最简单、零个性化零摩擦；人口画像被动、零摩擦、中等个性化；引导选偏好最贴口味但要加一步问卷、可能降转化——个性化越高往往摩擦越大。
why_en: Popularity is simplest with zero personalization and zero friction; demographic is passive, zero friction, medium personalization; onboarding fits taste best but adds a step and can cut conversion — more personalization tends to mean more friction.
tradeoff: 个性化程度 vs 注册摩擦/转化损失（越贴口味通常越费用户力气）
options: 三者的个性化程度和用户摩擦其实完全一样，随便选哪一个效果都相同
热门兜底=零个性化零摩擦；人口画像=被动中等个性化；引导选偏好=最贴口味但加摩擦
引导选偏好零摩擦最省事最简单，热门兜底反而是三者里最贵最复杂的那个
人口画像需要用户主动答一长串偏好问卷、逐项打分排序，摩擦在三者里最高，用户易半途放弃
options_en: All three carry identical personalization and friction, so it truly doesn't matter which one you pick.
Popularity = zero personalization, zero friction; demographic = passive, medium personalization; onboarding = best taste fit but adds friction.
Onboarding is the frictionless, easiest one to run; popularity is actually the most expensive and complex of the three.
Demographic requires the user to actively answer a long preference survey and rank items, giving it the highest friction and the most drop-off of the three.
optionExplanations: 三者差别很大：个性化 热门<人口画像<引导，摩擦 热门=人口画像<引导，不能随便选。
对；这正是三条回退的定位——热门最粗最省事，人口画像被动中等，引导最贴但费用户力气。
反了：引导才是加摩擦的那个，热门兜底最简单不复杂。
反了：人口画像是被动映射零摩擦，引导才需要用户主动答题。
optionExplanations_en: They differ a lot: personalization popularity<demographic<onboarding, friction popularity=demographic<onboarding — not interchangeable.
Correct — that's the exact positioning: popularity is coarsest and easiest, demographic passive and medium, onboarding best-fitting but effortful.
Backwards: onboarding is the one that adds friction, and popularity is the simplest, not the most complex.
Backwards: demographic is a passive zero-friction mapping; onboarding is the one requiring active answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 注册流程里每加一步让用户流失的可能，onboarding 加步骤会降低注册转化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signup friction is the drop-off risk each added signup step brings; onboarding steps lower signup conversion.

q: 把新用户回退层「如何叠加」的顺序排好（从进来到交给个性化模型）：
q_en: Order how the new-user fallback layers stack (from arrival to handing off to personalization):
steps: 引导选偏好在候选里重排，把用户亲手挑的兴趣顶上来
人口画像先缩小候选：映射到人群簇，取簇内偏好
积累约 5-20 次隐式交互后，交给协同过滤/学习嵌入接管
热门兜底填满剩余槽位，保证列表不空
why: 级联是优雅降级：先用人口画像缩小候选，再用用户挑的兴趣重排，热门填满剩余槽，最后随交互积累切给 CF——不是开/关二值，而是随数据逐层让位。
why_en: The cascade is graceful degradation: demographics narrow candidates, onboarding re-ranks, popularity fills the rest, then CF takes over as interactions accrue — not on/off but layers yielding as data grows.
diagram:
flowchart LR D["1 人口画像
缩小候选"] --> O["2 引导选偏好
重排"] O --> P["3 热门兜底
填满槽位"] P --> C["4 积累 5-20 交互
切到 CF"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据越少能力越弱但仍出结果，而不是数据不够就直接罢工，回退级联即此思路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation means capability weakens as data shrinks but still returns results, rather than failing outright — the idea behind the fallback cascade.

q: 新用户从「冷」转「暖」通常要多少次隐式交互，这个数字在设计里做什么用？
q_en: How many implicit interactions typically turn a new user from cold to warm, and what is that number used for?
why: 约 5-20 次隐式交互（点击/停留/跳过）后信号就够了，把他从回退层切到 CF/学习嵌入；这是给定的经验阈值（切换触发器），决定「何时停用兜底」，不是公式算出来的。
why_en: About 5-20 implicit interactions (clicks, dwell, skips) provide enough signal to switch him from fallback to CF/learned embeddings; it's a given rule-of-thumb threshold (a transition trigger) deciding when to stop the fallback, not a computed value.
options: 只要 1 次交互，点一下就立刻切到 CF
约 5-20 次隐式交互后切到 CF，是停用回退的触发阈值
至少 5,000 次才够，在那之前一直纯热门兜底
无需任何交互，注册当天就切到 CF
options_en: Just 1 interaction — a single click switches straight to CF.
About 5-20 implicit interactions before switching to CF -- the trigger for when to stop the fallback.
At least 5,000 before it's enough; until then it's pure popularity defaults.
No interactions needed; switch to CF on the signup day.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户不主动打分而通过点击/停留/跳过泄露的偏好，冷启动靠它逐步攒暖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Implicit signals are preferences leaked through clicks, dwell, and skips rather than explicit ratings, which cold start uses to warm up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定何时从回退切到个性化模型的阈值，常用交互次数或 embedding 置信度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transition trigger is the threshold deciding when to switch from fallback to personalization, usually interaction count or embedding confidence.

optionExplanations: 只点一次噪声很大，不足以说明真实偏好，太早切会让个性化跑偏。
对，5-20 次刚好能攒出稳定的隐式信号，切换点选得不算晚也不算莽撞。
等到 5,000 次早过了头，新用户会被晾在纯热门里太久，体验受损。
注册当天没有任何交互，CF 连相似度都算不出来，谈不上切换。
optionExplanations_en: One click is noisy and does not reveal real taste yet, so switching this early is premature.
Correct -- 5-20 interactions build a stable signal, not too early and not too late to switch.
Waiting for 5,000 leaves new users stuck on pure popularity far too long, hurting the experience.
Zero interactions on signup day give CF nothing to compute similarity from, so there is nothing to switch on.

scenario: 你想在注册流程加几步引导问卷来提升初始个性化。
scenario_en: You want to add a few onboarding survey steps to improve initial personalization.
q: 这么做的副作用是什么，标准的应对是什么？
q_en: What's the side effect, and what's the standard mitigation?
why: 引导每加一步都增加摩擦、降低注册转化；标准做法是 A/B 测试步骤数量，在「个性化质量 vs 注册流失」之间找平衡点。
why_en: Each onboarding step adds friction and cuts signup conversion; the standard move is to A/B test the number of steps, balancing personalization quality against drop-off.
options: 唯一副作用是增加服务器成本，多加几台机器就能彻底解决问题
会让协同过滤永久失效，应该干脆把 CF 整个关掉
每加一步都增加摩擦、降低转化；应 A/B 测步骤数找平衡
没有任何副作用，问卷步骤越多用户画像就越准，能加尽量都加上
options_en: The only side effect is higher server cost; just add a few more machines and it's fully solved.
It permanently breaks collaborative filtering, so you should just turn CF off entirely.
Each step adds friction and cuts signup conversion; A/B test the number of steps to balance personalization vs. drop-off.
There's no side effect at all — more survey steps only sharpen the profile, so add as many as you can.
optionExplanations: 服务器成本不是这里的机制，问题是用户会因步骤多而流失。
onboarding 和 CF 无关，更不会让 CF 失效，这个归因错了。
对；摩擦↔转化是核心取舍，用 A/B 找步骤数的甜点，正是标准做法。
错；步骤越多流失越大，个性化收益会被注册转化损失抵消。
optionExplanations_en: Server cost isn't the mechanism here; the issue is users dropping off from too many steps.
Onboarding is unrelated to CF and certainly doesn't break it; wrong attribution.
Correct — friction vs. conversion is the core trade-off, and A/B testing the step count to find the sweet spot is the standard move.
Wrong — more steps mean more drop-off, and personalization gains get offset by lost signup conversion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开始注册的人里最终完成注册的比例，onboarding 步骤越多它越容易下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signup conversion is the share of people who start signup and finish it; more onboarding steps tend to lower it.

scenario: 一个巴西、24 岁的新用户注册后直接跳过了引导问卷，此刻你要给他第一屏推荐。
scenario_en: A new user from Brazil, age 24, signs up and immediately skips the onboarding survey; you must fill his first screen of recommendations.
q: 最合理的冷启动策略是什么？
q_en: What's the most sensible cold-start strategy?
why: 他跳过了 onboarding，就退到被动信号：用注册信息把他映射到「巴西 / 18-25」人群簇，推该簇的热门曲目，等积累 10+ 次交互后切到协同过滤。
why_en: Since he skipped onboarding, fall back to passive signals: map him to a 'Brazil / 18-25' cluster, serve the cluster's top tracks, then switch to collaborative filtering after 10+ interactions.
tradeoff: 跳过 onboarding → 用人口画像被动兜底 vs 认真做 onboarding → 用亲手挑的兴趣重排
options: 首屏什么都不推，先晾着等他自己搜索产生交互再说
用注册信号映射到「巴西/18-25」人群簇，推簇内热门，攒够交互后切 CF
直接上协同过滤做推荐，反正交互矩阵里总能借到别的用户历史数据来算
强制他必须先做完引导问卷才能进入主页浏览
options_en: Show nothing on the first screen and just wait for him to search and generate interactions.
Map registration signals to a 'Brazil / 18-25' cluster, serve cluster top tracks, then switch to CF after 10+ interactions.
Go straight to CF — the interaction matrix always has some other user's data to borrow.
Force him to finish the onboarding survey before he can even browse the home page.
whenOtherWins: 如果他没跳过、认真做了 onboarding，就该优先用他亲手挑的兴趣重排，而不是只靠人群簇的粗粒度偏好。
optionExplanations: 空着首屏是最差体验，冷启动的意义就是「没数据也先给有用结果」。
对；跳过 onboarding 就用被动人口画像兜底，攒够交互再切 CF，正是标准级联。
他自己的行是空的，CF 算不出他的相似度，别人的数据帮不上。
强制问卷会把跳过的人直接逼走，摩擦过大伤转化。
optionExplanations_en: A blank first screen is the worst experience; cold start exists precisely to return useful results with no data.
Correct — skipping onboarding means passive demographic fallback, then switch to CF once interactions accrue — the standard cascade.
His own row is empty, so CF can't compute his similarity; other people's data doesn't help him.
Forcing the survey drives away the very users who skipped it — too much friction, hurting conversion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按年龄/地区等把用户归入的群体，簇有已知偏好分布，供新用户借用作初始画像。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A demographic cluster groups users by age/region with a known preference distribution, borrowed as a new user's initial profile.

q: 一个刚上架、零交互的新物品，为什么协同过滤无法把它推荐出去？
q_en: For a just-listed item with zero interactions, why can't collaborative filtering surface it?
why: 它在交互矩阵里的列是空的，CF 靠「和它有共同交互的用户/物品」来传播推荐，没有交互就没有共现，无法被 CF 召回。
why_en: Its column in the interaction matrix is empty, and CF propagates recommendations via users/items that co-interact with it, so with no interactions there's no co-occurrence and CF can't retrieve it.
options: 它的交互列是空的，CF 靠共现传播推荐，没有交互就无法被召回
新物品的元数据没通过审核，被系统主动屏蔽
CF 只推销量前 100 的物品，是硬编码白名单
新物品的 embedding 维度和老物品不一致，无法比较
options_en: Its interaction column is empty, and CF propagates via co-occurrence, so with no interactions it can't be retrieved.
The new item's metadata failed review and the system actively blocks it.
CF only recommends the top-100 by sales — a hardcoded whitelist.
The new item's embedding dimension differs from old items and can't be compared.
optionExplanations: 对；空列 = 没有共现，CF 无法把它和任何交互关联，只能靠内容/探索兜底。
这是审核臆想，CF 失效的真正原因是缺交互不是被屏蔽。
CF 没有「只推前 100」的硬编码，它只是数学上需要交互数据。
embedding 维度都是统一的，问题在于新物品还没有可算的交互 embedding。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — an empty column means no co-occurrence, so CF can't tie it to any interaction and must defer to content/exploration.
That's imagined moderation; CF fails from missing interactions, not from being blocked.
CF has no 'top-100 only' hardcode; it just mathematically needs interaction data.
Embedding dimensions are uniform; the issue is the new item has no computable interaction embedding yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 物品在交互矩阵里还没有任何用户交互，CF 无法通过共现把它召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An empty column means an item has no user interactions in the matrix, so CF can't retrieve it via co-occurrence.

scenario: 一个视频刚上传、零播放，你想让它在「有任何观看之前」就能进入候选池被推出去。
scenario_en: A video was just uploaded with zero views; you want it in the candidate pool and recommendable before any views happen.
q: 主路径该用哪种冷启动技术？
q_en: Which cold-start technique is the primary path here?
why: 内容 bootstrapping（主路径）：从元数据和缩略图/音频提特征，算与暖物品的相似度，按邻近继承暖启动 embedding，上线即可进候选（YouTube 用元数据 + 缩略图 CNN + 频道历史）。
why_en: Content-based bootstrapping (primary): extract features from title/description/tags/thumbnail (CNN)/audio spectrogram, compute similarity to warm items, and let the new item inherit a warm-start embedding by proximity so it enters candidates immediately (YouTube uses metadata + thumbnail CNN + channel history).
tradeoff: 内容 bootstrapping（上线即服务，依赖元数据质量） vs bandit 探索（实测信号，消耗曝光）
options: 协同过滤：用它的历史观看数据找相似视频（但它零播放，列完全是空的）
内容 bootstrapping：从元数据和缩略图/音频提特征，继承暖启动 embedding
热门兜底：把它当全局热门推给所有用户看到（它其实还没热起来，凭空当热门完全说不过去）
等它自然积累够 50 次观看后再放进候选池（那样它永远也起不来）
options_en: CF: use its view history to find similar videos (but it has zero views and a completely empty column).
Content-based bootstrapping: extract features from metadata and thumbnail/audio, inherit a warm-start embedding by proximity.
Popularity default: serve it to every user as if it were globally popular (it isn't actually popular yet, so treating it as such doesn't hold up).
Wait until it naturally accrues 50 views before it enters the candidate pool (then it never gets a chance to start).
whenOtherWins: 如果元数据极其稀疏或不准（连标题都乱填），content-based 的 embedding 会很差，此时更该靠 bandit 探索去实测真实信号。
optionExplanations: 它零播放、列是空的，CF 没有输入，走不通。
对；靠内容特征算相似度，让新物品直接拿到一个可用的起始向量，不用等真实播放也能进候选池。
它还没热，把它硬当热门既不准也没依据，只是兜底不是主路径。
等 50 次观看会陷入「没曝光→没数据→永远进不了候选」的死循环。
optionExplanations_en: It has zero views and an empty column, so CF has no input and can't work.
Correct — computing similarity from content features gives the new item a usable starting vector right away, no real plays required to enter the candidate pool.
It isn't popular yet, so forcing it as popular is inaccurate and unjustified — a fallback, not the primary path.
Waiting for 50 views creates a 'no exposure → no data → never enters candidates' deadlock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从物品元数据/图像/音频提特征，算与暖物品相似度，让新物品按邻近继承暖启动 embedding。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-based bootstrapping extracts features from item metadata/image/audio, matches warm items, and lets a new item inherit a warm-start embedding by proximity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 卷积神经网络：从图像（缩略图）或音频频谱提取特征向量的常用模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) extracts feature vectors from images (thumbnails) or audio spectrograms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新物品不从零学，而是继承一个由内容相似度得到的初始向量，先能被推。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A warm-start embedding is an initial vector a new item inherits from content similarity instead of learning from scratch, so it can be recommended right away.

scenario: 你用内容 bootstrapping 给新物品算 embedding，但发现新上架商品的推荐质量普遍很差。
scenario_en: You use content-based bootstrapping to embed new items, but recommendation quality for newly listed products is consistently poor.
q: 最可能的根因是什么，怎么缓解？
q_en: What's the most likely root cause, and how do you mitigate it?
why: content-based 过度依赖元数据质量——描述稀疏/不准 → 提取的特征差 → embedding 差；缓解靠补全元数据（强制关键字段、用 CNN/多模态从图像音频补特征）或叠加 bandit 探索去实测。
why_en: Content-based over-relies on metadata quality — sparse/inaccurate descriptions give weak features and a poor embedding; mitigate by enriching metadata (require key fields, use CNN/multimodal features from image/audio) or layering bandit exploration to measure real signal.
options: 根子在元数据质量：描述越空越不准，内容特征就越弱；该补齐字段、上多模态，并用探索去验证真实反馈
问题出在协同过滤，是它的锅，直接把 CF 模块整个关掉就能解决
是 embedding 的向量维度被设置得太高了，做一次降维压缩处理后应该就能修好
只是当前用户规模太少，等平台用户变多以后它就会自动变好
options_en: Root cause is metadata quality: emptier, less accurate descriptions give weaker content features; fix by filling required fields, adding multimodal signal, and layering exploration to verify real feedback.
The problem lies with collaborative filtering; just turn the whole CF module off and it's solved.
The embedding's dimensionality is set too high; running a dimensionality-reduction pass fixes it.
It's simply that the current user base is too small; it fixes itself once the platform's user count grows.
optionExplanations: 对；这条路径的质量上限就是元数据本身——描述空、内容特征就弱，embedding 也跟着变差，得补字段/上多模态/加探索才治本。
问题出在新物品的内容特征，不是 CF；关 CF 与这个失败模式无关。
降维改变不了「输入特征本身就差」这件事，垃圾进垃圾出。
这是新物品问题不是新用户问题，用户变多不会自动修好一个描述稀疏的物品。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this path's quality ceiling is the metadata itself: emptier descriptions mean weaker content features and a worse embedding, so filling fields / adding multimodal signal / layering exploration is the real fix.
The problem is the new item's content features, not CF; turning CF off is unrelated to this failure mode.
Dimensionality reduction can't fix inherently weak input features — garbage in, garbage out.
This is a new-item problem, not new-user; more users won't auto-fix an item with sparse descriptions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标题/描述/标签是否完整准确，直接决定内容 bootstrapping 得到的 embedding 好坏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metadata quality — whether title/description/tags are complete and accurate — directly determines the quality of a content-bootstrapped embedding.

q: 「用 bandit 做探索」在新物品冷启动里具体做什么？
q_en: What exactly does 'exploration via bandits' do for new-item cold start?
why: 用 epsilon-greedy / Thompson sampling 把一小部分流量分给新物品，快速收集真实交互信号（Airbnb 用规则式探索加成，在有限窗口内加权新房源，并随数据积累衰减）。
why_en: Use epsilon-greedy / Thompson sampling to allocate a fraction of traffic to new items and gather real interaction signal fast (Airbnb boosts new listings for a limited window via a rule-based bonus that decays as data accrues).
options: 把 100% 流量都强制分给新物品，以此保证它一定被曝光到
只把流量都给老物品，等新物品自己慢慢被用户发现
用 epsilon-greedy/Thompson sampling 分一小部分流量给新物品收信号，随数据衰减
用 bandit 算法压缩每个 embedding 向量的存储空间大小，跟探索机制完全没有任何关系
options_en: Force 100% of traffic to new items, guaranteeing they get exposure this way.
Give all traffic only to old items and let new items slowly get discovered on their own.
Use epsilon-greedy/Thompson sampling to route a fraction of traffic to new items for signal, decaying as data accrues.
Use bandit algorithms to compress the storage size of each embedding vector — has nothing at all to do with exploration.
optionExplanations: 100% 全给新物品会把没验证的内容硬塞给所有用户，UX 崩，探索是「一小部分」不是全部。
只给老物品新物品永远起不来，探索的意义正是主动分一点流量出去。
对；bandit 用小比例流量试探新物品收集信号，Airbnb 的加成还随数据衰减，是标准做法。
bandit 是探索-利用的决策方法，不是存储压缩，归因错。
optionExplanations_en: 100% to new items forces unvetted content on everyone and wrecks UX; exploration is a fraction, not everything.
Giving traffic only to old items means new items never take off; exploration is precisely about deliberately routing some traffic out.
Correct — bandits probe new items with a small traffic share to collect signal, and Airbnb's boost even decays with data — the standard approach.
Bandits are an explore-exploit decision method, not storage compression — wrong attribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多臂老虎机：在「探索未知选项」和「利用已知最优」间分配尝试的决策框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bandit (multi-armed bandit) is a decision framework that allocates trials between exploring unknown options and exploiting the known best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以概率 ε 随机探索、以 1-ε 选当前最优，最简单的探索-利用策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon-greedy explores at random with probability epsilon and exploits the current best otherwise, the simplest explore-exploit strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个选项「是最优」的后验概率来采样分配流量，天然平衡探索与利用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson sampling allocates traffic by sampling from each option's posterior probability of being best, naturally balancing exploration and exploitation.

q: 给新物品分流量做探索时，探索比例过高或过低分别会怎样？
q_en: When allocating traffic to explore new items, what happens if the exploration fraction is too high or too low?
why: 太少 → 新物品拿不到曝光、一直默默无闻；太多 → 大量用户被喂没验证过的内容、UX 变差。要在「发现速度 vs 体验损失」之间平衡，这就是 explore-exploit 取舍。
why_en: Too little → new items get no exposure and stay obscure; too much → many users get unvetted content and UX degrades. Balance discovery speed against experience cost — the explore-exploit trade-off.
tradeoff: 探索（加速发现新内容） vs 利用（保住当前用户体验）
options: 探索太少→新品长期无人问津；太多→体验变差；核心在拿捏两者平衡点
无论太多还是太少都没什么影响，随便设一个探索比例即可，不用纠结
太少反而会让 UX 变差，太多才会让新物品无人问津（其实说反了方向）
这只影响存储成本大小，跟推荐质量好坏完全没关系
options_en: Too little exploration leaves new items unnoticed for good; too much degrades the experience; the core is balancing the two.
Whether the fraction is high or low makes no real difference; just pick any exploration rate and don't overthink it.
Too little actually degrades UX, and too much is what leaves new items unnoticed (this option has the direction backwards).
This only affects how much storage you use, and has nothing to do with recommendation quality at all.
optionExplanations: 对；这正是探索-利用取舍的两端——探索不足新品埋没，探索过度体验受损。
比例是关键旋钮，设错任一端都有明确代价，不能随便。
方向反了：探索太少是新品无人问津，太多才是 UX 变差。
探索比例直接决定用户看到多少未验证内容，影响的是推荐质量不是存储。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — these are the two ends of explore-exploit: too little buries new items, too much hurts experience.
The fraction is the key knob; getting either end wrong has a clear cost, so it isn't arbitrary.
Direction reversed: too little exploration leaves new items unnoticed; too much is what degrades UX.
The exploration fraction determines how much unvetted content users see, affecting recommendation quality, not storage.

termDefinitions.term: explore-exploit trade-off / 探索-利用取舍
termDefinitions.meaning: 在「试探未知以求长期最优」和「利用已知最优保当下体验」之间的权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The explore-exploit trade-off weighs probing the unknown for long-term optimum against exploiting the known best for present experience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户体验：这里指推荐列表让用户满意的程度，过度探索会拉低它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UX (User Experience) here is how satisfying the recommendation list is; over-exploration lowers it.

q: 新物品的两条路径——内容 bootstrapping 和 bandit 探索——分别解决什么，为什么要同时跑？
q_en: The two new-item paths — content-based bootstrapping and bandit exploration — each solve what, and why run both?
why: content-based 靠元数据立刻给出可用 embedding（上线即服务），bandit 靠分流量收集真实交互（解决数据积累）；一个「马上能用」、一个「加速攒数据」，互补所以并行。
why_en: Content-based gives a usable embedding immediately from metadata (serves at launch); bandits allocate traffic to gather real interactions (solves data accumulation) — one is 'usable now,' the other 'accrue data faster,' so they're complementary and run in parallel.
tradeoff: 内容 bootstrapping（立即可用，依赖元数据质量） vs bandit 探索（实测信号，消耗曝光）
diagram:
flowchart TB N["新物品（列空）"] --> CB["内容 bootstrapping
元数据→暖启动 embedding
上线即服务"] N --> BD["bandit 探索
分流量收真实信号
加速攒数据"] CB --> M["~50 次交互后
协同信号接管"] BD --> M
options: 两者其实完全等价，选一个用就行，同时跑两条纯属浪费资源
content-based 负责收集数据、bandit 负责提供初始 embedding，两者角色其实说反了
两者都要等到 50 次交互之后才会起作用，在那之前都完全不工作
两条路径分工不同：内容特征让新物品第零秒就能服务，bandit 把流量匀给它去攒真实反馈，二者同时开跑才不留空窗
options_en: They're fully equivalent; pick either one, and running both at once is a pure waste of resources.
Content-based collects the data while bandits supply the initial embedding — the roles are actually reversed here.
Both only kick in after 50 interactions and do absolutely nothing before that point.
The two paths split the work: content features let a new item serve from second zero, while bandits route traffic to gather real feedback — running both together avoids any dead gap.
optionExplanations: 两者解决的是不同问题（即时可用 vs 攒数据），不是重复，同时跑不是浪费。
反了：内容负责初始 embedding，bandit 负责收集数据。
对这条路径来说不成立——内容路径从上线第 0 秒就已经在服务，根本不用等到 50 次交互。
对；一个立刻能用、一个加速积累真实信号，正好互补，所以并行跑。
optionExplanations_en: They solve different problems (usable now vs. accrue data), not duplicates, so running both isn't wasteful.
Reversed: content-based supplies the initial embedding and bandits collect data.
Content-based serves from second zero, not after 50 interactions — this is wrong.
Correct — one is usable immediately, the other accelerates real-signal accrual, complementary, so they run in parallel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐管线的第一步，从海量物品里粗选出一批候选交给后续精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the first recommendation-pipeline step that coarsely selects a set of items from the full catalog for later ranking.

q: 新物品积累到大约多少次交互后，协同信号就可靠到能替换掉 bootstrapped embedding（即靠内容相似度算出的临时向量）？
q_en: After roughly how many interactions is the collaborative signal reliable enough to replace a new item's bootstrapped embedding (the temporary vector derived from content similarity)?
why: 约 50+ 次交互后协同信号足够可靠，可以从内容近似的 embedding 切到真实协同 embedding；这是给定的经验阈值（新物品切换触发器），比新用户的 5-20 高，因为要跨多个用户聚合信号。
why_en: After about 50+ interactions the collaborative signal is reliable enough to switch from the content-approximated embedding to the real collaborative one; it's a rule-of-thumb transition trigger, set higher than the new-user range, since signal must aggregate across many users.
options: 约 50+ 次交互后协同信号可靠，换掉 bootstrapped embedding
1 次交互就够，被看一次就切到协同 embedding
必须上百万次交互，之前一直用内容 embedding
永远不替换，新物品一直用内容 bootstrapped embedding
options_en: About 50+ interactions before the collaborative signal is reliable enough to replace the bootstrapped embedding.
Just 1 interaction — one view switches to the collaborative embedding.
Millions of interactions are required; until then it uses the content embedding.
Never replace it — a new item keeps its content-bootstrapped embedding forever.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新物品上线时由内容相似度临时得到的暖启动向量，交互攒够后被真实协同 embedding 替换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bootstrapped embedding is the temporary warm-start vector a new item gets from content similarity, later replaced by the real collaborative embedding once interactions accrue.

optionExplanations: 对，50+ 次能让协同信号跨足够多用户聚合，替换才靠谱。
只看一次的信号噪声极大，还撑不起协同判断，切换为时过早。
拖到上百万次太保守，白白浪费了内容 embedding 早该让位的窗口。
一直不换会让新物品永远吃不到更准的协同信号，个性化止步不前。
optionExplanations_en: Correct -- once you clear roughly 50 interactions, CF's pooled signal is trustworthy enough to swap in.
A single view is too noisy for CF to trust yet, so swapping this early is premature.
Waiting for millions is overly cautious -- the bootstrapped vector should hand off long before that.
Never swapping it means the item's ranking never benefits from real cross-user signal.

q: 「新系统冷启动」为什么是最极端的一类，什么场景一定会遇到？
q_en: Why is new-system cold start the most extreme type, and which scenario always hits it?
why: 新系统三无：没有用户、没有带数据的物品、没有训练好的模型——连回退所依赖的暖数据都没有；每个从零起步的创业公司都会遇到，是常见的 Staff+ 面试题。
why_en: A new system has none of the three: no users, no items with data, no trained model — not even the warm data fallbacks rely on; every from-scratch startup hits it, a common Staff+ interview question.
options: 只是新用户冷启动的另一个说法而已，本质没有任何区别
只在系统迁移、更换数据库时才会出现的临时状况
指的是模型服务器冷启动延迟过高的那类基础设施运维问题，跟推荐无关
三无：没用户、没带数据的物品、没模型；从零起步的创业公司都会遇到
options_en: Just another name for new-user cold start; fundamentally there's no difference at all.
Only appears as a temporary situation during system migration or a database swap.
Refers to the infrastructure issue of excessive model-server cold-start latency, unrelated to recommendations.
None of the three — no users, no items with data, no model; every from-scratch startup runs into it.
optionExplanations: 新系统不止用户冷，物品和模型也全无，比新用户严重得多。
迁移只是换后端，用户/物品数据还在，不是新系统冷启动。
那是 serverless 延迟，另一个同名概念，不是推荐冷启动。
对；三无是它区别于其他两类的本质，绿地创业必遇，Staff+ 常考。
optionExplanations_en: A new system is more than user-cold; items and model are also absent, far worse than new-user.
Migration just swaps the backend; user/item data still exists, so it isn't new-system cold start.
That's serverless latency, a same-name concept, not recommendation cold start.
Correct — having none of the three is what distinguishes it, hit by every greenfield startup and common at Staff+.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从零起步、没有任何历史数据或系统的全新项目，是新系统冷启动的典型场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Greenfield means a brand-new project built from scratch with no prior data or system, the classic new-system cold-start scenario.

scenario: 一个全新平台刚上线，还没有任何数据训练第一个模型，但首页不能空着。
scenario_en: A brand-new platform just launched with no data to train a first model, but the home page can't be empty.
q: 用什么当「初始策略」把系统先跑起来？
q_en: What initial policy do you use to get the system running?
why: 规则式预热（rule-based warming）：用手工启发式（编辑精选、按新近度、供给方质量分）当初始策略，一边服务一边收集数据训练第一个模型。
why_en: Rule-based warming: use hand-crafted heuristics (editorial curation, recency, supplier quality scores) as the initial policy while collecting data to train a first model.
tradeoff: 规则式预热（无需数据，起点低但立刻能用） vs 迁移学习（借相邻域，起点高但要有可迁的源）
options: 规则式预热：用编辑精选/新近度/质量分等启发式当初始策略，边服务边收集数据
直接上协同过滤来做推荐（但压根没有任何交互数据可用）
要等攒够足够多的数据、训练好模型之后才上线（首页会一直空着没内容）
纯随机推荐给用户，反正现在没有任何数据可参考
options_en: Rule-based warming: use heuristics (editorial curation, recency, supplier quality scores) as the initial policy while collecting data.
Go straight to CF for recommendations (but there's simply no interaction data to use at all).
Wait until enough data accrues to train a model before launching (the home page stays empty the whole time).
Serve purely random recommendations, since there's no data to reference right now anyway.
whenOtherWins: 如果已有一个相邻域的成熟模型/数据（如已有音乐推荐要上播客），用迁移学习会比纯手工规则起点更高。
optionExplanations: 对；没有数据时手工规则是唯一能立刻上线又比随机强的初始策略，边跑边攒数据。
CF 需要交互数据，新系统一条都没有，走不通。
等模型训好首页会一直空，用户流失，违背「不能空着」。
纯随机比规则差得多，编辑精选/新近度等启发式明显更有信息量。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with no data, hand-crafted rules are the only initial policy that launches now and beats random, accruing data as it runs.
CF needs interaction data, and a new system has none, so it can't work.
Waiting for a trained model leaves the home page empty and users leave, violating 'can't be empty.'
Pure random is far worse than rules; heuristics like editorial curation/recency are clearly more informative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用手工启发式（编辑精选/新近度/供给质量）当初始推荐策略，同时收集数据训练首个模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rule-based warming uses hand-crafted heuristics (editorial curation/recency/supplier quality) as the initial policy while collecting data to train a first model.

scenario: Spotify 要给一个全新的「播客」品类做推荐，但播客侧还没有任何用户行为数据。
scenario_en: Spotify wants recommendations for a brand-new podcast category, but there's no user behavior data on the podcast side yet.
q: 怎么给这个新品类一个高起点？
q_en: How do you give this new category a strong starting point?
why: 迁移学习：把播客元数据映射进已有的「音乐内容特征空间」，复用成熟域的表示，避免从零起步（Spotify 就是这样 warm-start 播客推荐的）。
why_en: Transfer learning: map podcast metadata into the existing music content feature space, reusing the mature domain's representation to avoid starting from scratch (this is how Spotify warm-started podcast recs).
tradeoff: 迁移学习（借成熟域表示，起点高） vs 规则式预热（无源可迁时的兜底，起点低）
options: 给播客单独从零训练一个新模型，完全不碰音乐现有那一套
用音乐的协同过滤矩阵直接拿来推播客（矩阵里根本没有播客的列数据）
迁移学习：把播客元数据映射进已有的音乐内容特征空间，复用成熟表示避免从零
等播客自己慢慢攒够播放量之后再开始做推荐
options_en: Train a brand-new model for podcasts entirely from scratch, without touching the existing music stack at all.
Use the music CF matrix directly to recommend podcasts (there's simply no podcast column data in it at all).
Transfer learning: map podcast metadata into the existing music content feature space, reusing the mature representation to avoid starting from scratch.
Just wait until podcasts slowly accrue enough plays on their own before starting any recommendation.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有任何相邻的成熟域可借（真正的绿地创业），迁移无源可迁，只能退到规则式预热。
optionExplanations: 从零单训会白白浪费已有的成熟内容特征空间，起点低得多。
音乐 CF 矩阵里没有播客的列，直接套用无从谈起。
对；把新品类元数据映射进成熟特征空间正是迁移学习，起点远高于从零。
干等播放量会让新品类长期没有可用推荐，违背「高起点」的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Training from scratch wastes the existing mature content feature space and starts far lower.
The music CF matrix has no podcast column, so directly reusing it is a non-starter.
Correct — mapping the new category's metadata into a mature feature space is exactly transfer learning, starting far above scratch.
Idly waiting for plays leaves the new category without usable recs for a long time, missing the 'strong start' goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个成熟域学到的表示迁到数据稀缺的新域，让新域不必从零学起。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transfer learning ports a representation learned in a mature domain to a data-scarce new domain so it needn't learn from scratch.

scenario: 生产级推荐系统要同时处理暖用户暖物品、冷用户、冷物品这三种混合流量。
scenario_en: A production recommender must simultaneously handle warm users/items, cold users, and cold items in mixed traffic.
q: Netflix 式的混合架构怎么组织这些模型？
q_en: How does a Netflix-style hybrid architecture organize these models?
why: 级联：CF 服务暖用户暖物品 + content-based 服务冷物品 + 热门兜底服务冷用户；服务层按每个 user-item 对的数据可得性动态挑用哪个模型，而不是给用户固定绑一个模型。
why_en: Cascade: CF serves warm users/items + content-based serves cold items + popularity serves cold users; the serving layer picks the model per user-item pair by data availability rather than binding one model per user.
tradeoff: 按 user-item 对动态选模型（数据可得性驱动） vs 每用户静态绑一个模型（简单但错配冷/暖）
diagram:
flowchart TB
  REQ["user-item 对"] --> SL{"服务层：按数据可得性选模型"}
  SL -->|"暖用户暖物品"| CF["协同过滤"]
  SL -->|"冷物品"| CB["内容 based"]
  SL -->|"冷用户"| POP["热门兜底"]
options: 级联：暖用户暖物品用 CF、冷物品用 content-based、冷用户用热门，按数据可得性挑模型
整个系统只用一个协同过滤模型来处理暖用户暖物品、冷用户和冷物品的所有请求
给每个用户在系统里固定绑死一个模型，之后无论遇到冷热物品都永不切换
按物品的类别静态分配固定模型，这跟每个 user-item 对的数据是否充足完全没有关系
options_en: Cascade: warm users/items use CF, cold items use content-based, cold users use popularity — the serving layer picks per user-item pair by data availability.
The entire system uses a single collaborative-filtering model to handle every warm and cold user-item request.
Bind each user in the system to one fixed model permanently, and never switch it regardless of which items they hit.
Statically assign models by item category, which has nothing at all to do with whether each user-item pair has enough data.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统还处于新系统阶段（连暖数据都没有），级联里没有 CF 可用，得先靠规则预热/迁移学习把整套撑起来。
optionExplanations: 对；不同 user-item 对数据状况不同，服务层按可得性动态选模型，正是生产混合架构。
单 CF 处理不了冷用户/冷物品，它们的行列是空的。
用户会同时遇到冷物品和暖物品，固定绑一个模型必然错配。
该按数据可得性选而非物品类别；类别一样但数据冷暖不同就该走不同模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — different user-item pairs have different data states, so the serving layer picks the model by availability, exactly the production hybrid.
A single CF can't handle cold users/items whose rows/columns are empty.
A user meets both cold and warm items, so binding one fixed model necessarily mismatches.
Selection should follow data availability, not item category; same category with different data warmth needs different models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上按每个 user-item 对的数据可得性动态选择用哪个推荐模型的调度层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving layer is the online dispatch that picks which recommendation model to use per user-item pair by data availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个模型（CF/内容/热门）按数据充足度分层组合，数据越少退得越靠底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascade layers multiple models (CF/content/popularity) by data sufficiency, falling to lower layers as data shrinks.

q: Spotify Discover Weekly 怎么同时处理暖用户和全新曲目？
q_en: How does Spotify Discover Weekly handle both warm users and brand-new tracks?
why: 暖用户用矩阵分解（matrix factorization）走协同信号，新曲目用 CNN 分析音频频谱做内容分析，并随交互积累动态把权重从「内容」逐渐移向「协同」。
why_en: Warm users go through matrix factorization for collaborative signal, new tracks get CNN spectrogram content analysis, and weight dynamically shifts from content toward collaborative as interactions accrue.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["新曲目：CNN 音频频谱内容分析"] -->|"交互积累
权重内容→协同"| B["暖曲目：矩阵分解协同信号"]
options: 全部都只用矩阵分解来处理，连全新曲目也用同一套逻辑
暖用户走矩阵分解，新曲目走 CNN 频谱分析，权重随数据由内容移向协同
全部都只用 CNN 频谱来做音频分析处理曲目，完全不用任何协同信号
用编辑精选覆盖所有曲目来推荐，完全不做任何个性化处理
options_en: Use only matrix factorization for everything, applying the same logic even to brand-new tracks.
Warm users go through matrix factorization, new tracks go through CNN spectrogram analysis, and weight shifts from content toward collaborative as data grows.
Use only CNN spectrogram audio analysis for every track, with no collaborative signal used at all.
Cover every track with editorial curation for recommendations, doing no personalization whatsoever.
optionExplanations: 矩阵分解处理不了零交互的新曲目，它们的列是空的，需要内容分析补。
对；MF 走协同、CNN 走内容，权重随数据从内容移向协同，是动态混合的范例。
只用 CNN 会丢掉暖曲目已有的丰富协同信号，个性化会变差。
纯编辑精选零个性化，和 Discover Weekly 的个性化目标相反。
optionExplanations_en: Matrix factorization can't handle zero-interaction new tracks with empty columns; content analysis fills that gap.
Correct — MF for collaborative, CNN for content, weight shifting from content to collaborative as data grows, a dynamic-hybrid exemplar.
Only CNN discards warm tracks' rich collaborative signal, degrading personalization.
Pure editorial curation is zero personalization, opposite to Discover Weekly's personalized goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户-物品交互矩阵分解成用户向量×物品向量，是协同过滤的经典实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Matrix factorization decomposes the user-item matrix into user and item vectors, a classic collaborative-filtering implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把音频随时间的频率能量画成图，CNN 可从中提取曲目的内容特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spectrogram plots audio frequency energy over time, from which a CNN extracts a track's content features.

q: 把「在面试里讨论冷启动」的 4 步法排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 4-step method for discussing cold start in an interview:
steps: 阐明转换机制：以交互次数或 embedding 置信度设阈值
识别适用的冷启动类型：成熟平台+新品类=新物品；绿地=三种全有
处理失败模式：内容依赖元数据、人口画像编码偏见、规则跟不上新偏好
设计回退级联：每个数据水平下系统做什么（优雅降级，不是开/关二值）
why: 先识别哪几类冷启动适用，再设计逐层降级的回退级联，然后讲清何时从回退切到模型（转换机制），最后主动点出失败模式——这条顺序展示的是系统性思考而非背套路。
why_en: First identify which cold-start types apply, then design the graceful-degradation fallback cascade, then articulate when to switch from fallback to model (the transition), and finally call out failure modes — this order shows systematic thinking, not a memorized script.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  S1["1 识别适用类型"] --> S2["2 设计回退级联"]
  S2 --> S3["3 阐明转换机制"]
  S3 --> S4["4 处理失败模式"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定何时从回退切到个性化模型的规则，通常是交互次数阈值或 embedding 置信度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transition mechanism is the rule for when to switch from fallback to the personalization model, usually an interaction-count threshold or embedding confidence.

scenario: 一个成熟的视频平台（海量老用户、海量老视频）刚开放「上传新剧集」这个新品类。
scenario_en: A mature video platform (tons of existing users and videos) just opened a new content type: uploading new series.
q: 该主要考虑哪一类冷启动？
q_en: Which cold-start type should you mainly consider?
why: 只有新物品冷启动——用户和平台都是暖的，只有新上架的剧集列是空的；不需要处理新用户或新系统，这就是「成熟平台 + 新品类 = 物品冷启动」。
why_en: Only new-item cold start — users and platform are warm, only the new series' columns are empty; no need to handle new-user or new-system, i.e. 'mature platform + new content type = item cold start.'
tradeoff: 成熟平台+新品类（只有新物品冷） vs 绿地发布（三种全有）
options: 三种全都算冷，因为任何新东西上线都要从零开始起步
新系统冷启动，因为平台多了一个全新的内容品类
完全没有冷启动，成熟平台不会受到任何影响
只有新物品冷启动：用户和平台都暖，只有新剧集的列是空的
options_en: All three, because anything new launching always has to start completely from scratch.
New-system cold start, because the platform added a brand-new content category.
No cold start at all — a mature platform is completely unaffected.
Only new-item cold start: users and platform are warm, only the new series' columns are empty.
whenOtherWins: 如果这是从零发布的绿地产品而非成熟平台加品类，那就三种全有，得把整套回退 + 规则预热都上。
optionExplanations: 用户和平台都暖，不是三种全有；只有新剧集是冷的。
新增品类不等于新系统，平台的用户和模型都还在，不是三无。
新剧集列是空的，CF 推不出去，确实存在新物品冷启动。
对；成熟平台上新品类的经典判断——只有新物品冷，用户/系统都暖。
optionExplanations_en: Users and platform are warm, so it's not all three; only the new series are cold.
Adding a category isn't a new system; the platform's users and model still exist, so not all-three-absent.
The new series' columns are empty and CF can't surface them, so new-item cold start does exist.
Correct — the classic mature-platform-plus-new-category judgment: only new-item cold, users/system warm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平台上一类新的物品形态（如视频平台新增剧集/播客），常引入新物品冷启动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A content type is a new class of item on a platform (e.g. series/podcasts on a video platform), which typically introduces new-item cold start.

q: 讨论冷启动的失败模式时，以下哪些是必须点名的真实风险（多选）？
q_en: When discussing cold-start failure modes, which are real risks worth naming (select all)?
why: 三大失败模式：content-based 在元数据稀疏/不准时失效、人口画像会编码历史偏见、规则式预热跟不上新兴/突发偏好。「回退层写满数据库要每天清空」是编造的干扰项。
why_en: Three failure modes: content-based fails on sparse/inaccurate metadata, demographic fallbacks encode historical bias, and rule-based warming can't adapt to emergent preferences; 'the fallback layer fills the database and must be wiped daily' is a fabricated distractor.
options: content-based 在元数据稀疏/不准时失效，embedding 变差
人口画像会编码历史偏见，把群体刻板印象当个人偏好
规则式预热跟不上新兴/突发的偏好变化
回退层用久了会把数据库写满，必须每天清空
options_en: Content-based fails on sparse/inaccurate metadata, giving a poor embedding.
Demographic fallbacks encode historical bias, treating group stereotypes as individual preference.
Rule-based warming can't adapt to emergent or sudden preference shifts.
The fallback layer fills the database over time and must be wiped daily.
optionExplanations: 对；content-based 的质量被元数据封顶，描述烂 embedding 就烂，是首要失败模式。
对；人口画像把人群先验强加到个人，会固化历史偏见，是必须点名的伦理风险。
对；手工规则是静态的，接不住突发流行/新偏好，是它的天生短板。
编造的运维臆想；回退层不会「写满数据库要每天清空」，与失败模式无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — content-based quality is capped by metadata, so bad descriptions give bad embeddings, the primary failure mode.
Correct — demographic profiling imposes group priors on individuals and can entrench historical bias, an ethical risk worth naming.
Correct — hand-crafted rules are static and can't catch sudden trends or new preferences, an inherent weakness.
A fabricated ops claim; the fallback layer doesn't 'fill the database and need daily wiping,' unrelated to failure modes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 突然流行、历史规则没覆盖的新口味，静态规则式预热往往接不住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An emergent preference is a suddenly popular taste not covered by historical rules, which static rule-based warming often misses.

scenario: 你用人口画像给新用户做初始推荐，把性别/年龄/地区映射到人群簇的偏好分布。
scenario_en: You use demographic profiling for new users, mapping gender/age/region to a cluster's preference distribution.
q: 这条回退的伦理/质量风险是什么，怎么缓解？
q_en: What's the ethical/quality risk of this fallback, and how do you mitigate it?
why: 它会编码历史偏见——把群体刻板印象当成个人偏好（如按性别默认推某类内容）；缓解靠尽快用个人隐式信号覆盖人群先验、审计簇偏好、限制敏感属性的权重。
why_en: It encodes historical bias — treating group stereotypes as individual preference (e.g. defaulting content by gender); mitigate by overriding the group prior with personal implicit signals fast, auditing cluster preferences, and capping the weight of sensitive attributes.
options: 它编码历史偏见：群体刻板印象被当成个人偏好；应尽快用隐式信号覆盖先验
唯一的风险是计算速度变慢，只要加个缓存层就能轻松解决
会让协同过滤模型永久性失效，所以应该干脆把 CF 整个模块关掉
没有任何风险，人口画像在任何情况下都是最优选择
options_en: It encodes historical bias — group stereotypes get treated as individual preference; the fix is overriding the prior with personal signals fast.
The only risk is that computation gets slower; just adding a cache layer easily solves it.
It permanently breaks the collaborative-filtering model, so you should just shut the entire CF module down.
There's no risk at all; demographic profiling is always the optimal choice no matter the situation.
optionExplanations: 对；人群先验会把刻板印象套到个人身上，缓解的关键是尽快让个人信号接管并审计敏感属性。
计算慢不是这里的机制，真正的风险是偏见被编码进推荐。
人口画像和 CF 无关，更不会让它失效，归因错。
它明显有偏见风险，且只在没有个人数据时才用，不是「总是最优」。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the group prior imposes stereotypes on individuals, and the key mitigation is letting personal signal take over fast and auditing sensitive attributes.
Slow computation isn't the mechanism; the real risk is bias getting encoded into recommendations.
Demographic profiling is unrelated to CF and doesn't break it — wrong attribution.
It clearly carries bias risk and is used only absent personal data, so it's not 'always optimal.'

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练/人群数据里沿袭下来的系统性偏差，人口画像会把它当默认偏好强加给个人。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Historical bias is systematic skew inherited from training/population data, which demographic profiling can impose on individuals as a default preference.

q: 冷启动策略该监控哪些指标来判断回退是否真的有效（多选）？
q_en: Which metrics should you monitor to tell whether the cold-start fallback actually works (select all)?
why: 监控是策略的一部分：新用户看 Day-1 留存（回退给的初体验够不够好）、新物品看首周 CTR（内容/探索是否让它被发现）、再看用户/物品从「回退→模型推荐」的迁移速率（冷→暖是否顺畅）。
why_en: Monitoring is part of the strategy: Day-1 retention for new users (is the fallback's first experience good enough), first-week CTR for new items (do content/exploration surface them), and the fallback→model migration rate (is cold→warm smooth).
options: 新用户的 Day-1 留存：回退是否给了够好的初体验
新物品的首周 CTR：内容 bootstrapping/探索是否让它被发现
用户/物品从「回退」迁移到「模型推荐」的速率：冷→暖是否顺畅
数据库磁盘占用率：与冷启动效果无关的干扰
options_en: Day-1 retention for new users: does the fallback give a good enough first experience.
First-week CTR for new items: do content bootstrapping/exploration get them discovered.
Rate at which users/items migrate from fallback to model-based recs: is cold→warm smooth.
Database disk utilization: unrelated to cold-start effectiveness — a distractor.
optionExplanations: 对；Day-1 留存直接反映新用户的冷启动初体验好不好。
对；首周 CTR 反映新物品有没有被内容/探索成功推出去。
对；迁移速率衡量冷实体转暖的顺畅度，是冷启动健康度的核心信号。
磁盘占用是基础设施指标，跟回退是否有效无关，属干扰项。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — Day-1 retention directly reflects whether the new user's cold-start first experience is good.
Correct — first-week CTR reflects whether content/exploration successfully surface a new item.
Correct — migration rate measures how smoothly cold entities warm up, a core cold-start health signal.
Disk utilization is an infra metric unrelated to fallback effectiveness — a distractor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户注册后第 1 天回访的比例，用来衡量冷启动初体验的质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Day-1 retention is the share of new users who return the day after signup, gauging the quality of the cold-start first experience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例，新物品首周 CTR 反映它是否被成功推出去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of impressions clicked; a new item's first-week CTR shows whether it's being surfaced.

q: 新用户约 5-20 次交互就切到 CF，新物品要 ~50+ 次才切到协同信号——这个差异对设计意味着什么？
q_en: New users switch to CF at ~5-20 interactions, new items only at ~50+ — what does that gap imply for design?
why: 新用户的每次交互都直接暴露「他自己」的口味，信号密度高，少量就够；新物品要在多个不同用户身上被交互才能定位它在协同空间的位置，需要更多样本。所以物品侧的回退（content-based + 探索）要撑更久、探索预算要更足。
why_en: Each new-user interaction directly reveals his own taste — high signal density, so few suffice; a new item must be interacted with by many different users to locate its place in collaborative space, needing more samples. So the item-side fallback (content-based + exploration) must last longer with a larger exploration budget.
tradeoff: 新用户阈值低（信号来自单人高密度） vs 新物品阈值高（信号要跨多用户聚合）
options: 这纯粹是工程师拍脑袋随便定的两个数字，完全没有任何设计含义可言
用户信号单人高密度少量就够；物品信号要跨多用户聚合，需更多样本，回退要撑更久
新物品的阈值其实应该定得更低才对，因为物品的数量本来就比用户数量多得多
两个阈值应该统一合并成同一个数值，这样能大大简化系统
options_en: This is purely an engineer's arbitrary pick for the two numbers, carrying no design meaning at all.
User signal is single-person and dense, so a few suffice; item signal must aggregate across many users, needing more samples, so the item-side fallback runs longer.
The new-item threshold should actually be set lower, since the number of items far exceeds the number of users.
The two thresholds should be merged into one unified value, which would greatly simplify the system.
optionExplanations: 两个数字有明确成因和设计含义，不是拍脑袋——信号密度不同决定阈值不同。
对；用户信号是单人高密度、物品信号要跨多用户聚合，所以物品阈值更高、回退和探索都要撑更久。
数量多少不决定阈值；物品阈值更高是因为它的协同信号更难攒齐，不是因为物品多。
强行统一会让其中一侧要么过早切（不准）要么过晚切（浪费回退），不能简化了事。
optionExplanations_en: The two numbers have clear causes and design meaning, not arbitrary — differing signal density sets differing thresholds.
Correct — user signal is single-person dense while item signal must aggregate across users, so the item threshold is higher and its fallback/exploration must last longer.
Count doesn't set the threshold; the item threshold is higher because its collaborative signal is harder to accrue, not because items are numerous.
Forcing one number makes one side switch too early (inaccurate) or too late (wasted fallback); you can't simplify it away.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单次交互携带多少可用偏好信息；用户侧高（暴露本人口味），物品侧低（要跨多人聚合）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signal density is how much usable preference info one interaction carries; high user-side (reveals one's taste), low item-side (must aggregate across people).

q: 新系统冷启动什么时候才能训练出第一个真正的模型？
q_en: When can a new-system cold start finally train its first real model?
why: 当全系统累计的交互量达到能支撑首次训练时才行；在那之前靠规则式预热 + 迁移学习撑着，一边服务一边攒数据，这就是新系统的转换触发器。
why_en: Only once system-wide interaction volume is enough to support a first training run; until then rule-based warming + transfer learning carry it while serving and accruing data — the new-system transition trigger.
options: 系统上线的第一天就已经能训练出一个完全可用的推荐模型
永远都训练不出来，只能一直靠人工规则硬撑下去
当全系统交互量够支撑首次训练时；之前靠规则+迁移学习撑着攒数据
只要有一个用户完成注册就立刻能开始训练
options_en: The system can already train a fully usable recommendation model on day one of launch.
It can never train at all and must lean on hand-crafted rules forever.
Once system-wide interaction volume can support a first training run; until then rules + transfer learning carry it while accruing data.
As soon as a single user finishes signing up, training can begin right away.
optionExplanations: 第一天零交互，训练不了；得先靠规则/迁移攒数据。
并非永远训不了，攒够全系统交互量后就能训第一个模型。
对；新系统的转换触发器是「全系统交互量够训练」，之前用规则+迁移过渡。
一个用户的数据远不足以训练，样本量太小会严重过拟合。
optionExplanations_en: Day one has zero interactions, so training is impossible; rules/transfer must accrue data first.
It's not never; once system-wide interaction volume is enough, the first model can train.
Correct — the new-system transition trigger is 'system-wide volume sufficient to train,' bridged by rules + transfer before then.
One user's data is far too little to train; such a tiny sample severely overfits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全系统累计的用户-物品交互总数，达到一定规模才够训练第一个模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interaction volume is the system-wide total of user-item interactions, which must reach a certain scale to train a first model.

q: 补全冷启动的三种类型，以及回退层坐在哪个模型之下：
q_en: Fill in the three cold-start types and which model the fallback layer sits beneath:
text: 冷启动三种类型：{{新用户}}（矩阵的行空）、{{新物品}}（矩阵的列空）、{{新系统}}（无用户、无物品数据、无模型）；回退层永久地坐在{{协同过滤}}和学习嵌入的下面。
text_en: Three cold-start types: {{new user}} (empty matrix row), {{new item}} (empty matrix column), {{new system}} (no users, item data, or model); the fallback layer sits permanently beneath {{collaborative filtering}} and learned embeddings.
why: 三类分别对应矩阵的行空、列空、整张矩阵都空；回退层不是临时补丁，而是常驻在 CF/嵌入之下的永久架构层。
why_en: The three types map to an empty row, an empty column, and an empty matrix; the fallback isn't a hack but a permanent layer resident beneath CF/embeddings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从交互数据训练出的用户/物品向量表示，和协同过滤同属数据充足时的个性化层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned embeddings are user/item vector representations trained from interaction data, forming the data-rich personalization layer alongside collaborative filtering.

q: 补全新物品冷启动的两条并行路径和切换阈值：
q_en: Fill in the new item's two parallel paths and the switch threshold:
text: 新物品有两条并行路径：{{内容}} bootstrapping 靠元数据立刻给暖启动 embedding，{{探索}}（epsilon-greedy/Thompson sampling）分流量收真实信号；约 {{50}} 次交互后协同信号接管。
text_en: A new item runs two parallel paths: {{content}}-based bootstrapping gives a warm-start embedding from metadata immediately, while {{exploration}} (epsilon-greedy/Thompson sampling) allocates traffic for real signal; after about {{50}} interactions the collaborative signal takes over.
why: 内容路径解决「马上能用」，探索路径解决「加速攒数据」，两者并行；攒到约 50 次交互协同信号就可靠到能替换掉 bootstrapped embedding。
why_en: The content path solves 'usable now,' the exploration path solves 'accrue data faster,' running in parallel; after ~50 interactions the collaborative signal is reliable enough to replace the bootstrapped embedding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容 bootstrapping 与 bandit 探索同时运行，一个立即服务、一个加速攒数据，互补。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Parallel paths run content-based bootstrapping and bandit exploration at once — one serves immediately, the other accelerates data accrual — complementary.
